title: New "accessible-autofocus" attribute

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? The autofocus attribute has accessibility concerns, in that autofocus on a given form control means that the reading of the page items before the autofocused control get skipped over by screen readers. For example, a login page having autofocus on the LoginID like the example below only reads (NVDA, using Microsoft Edge): `Login ID: edit has auto complete blank` all of the items before the input for the Login ID are not read, and neither is anything after it. Example login form: ```

Welcome to the login page!

Login using the form below

Below is an exciting and simplified form that omits a lot for this example

``` ### What solutions exist today? As far as I've seen, the only ways to solve this issue are to not use it at all, or use some kind of time delay using JavaScript. ### How would you solve it? I would solve it by implementing an "accessible-autofocus" attribute that would add to what a screen reader sees among its list of items, and it would prevent the content before it from getting skipped over and the content afterwards from being omitted entirely. This would better mimic what a sighted user has access to, and enables the user of the screen reader to be aware of the focus location rather than being forced to it without any ability on their part to deal with it before it knowing anything else about the page. In the HTML above, swapping out the "autofocus" attribute with "accessible-autofocus" would allow screen readers to allow the person hearing the reader to know where the focus is currently without sacrificing the preceding content. Other regular autofocus behavior would apply visually as it does now. In this situation, the screen reader would still read: ``` heading level 1 Welcome to the login page heading level 2 Login using the form below Below is an exciting and simplified form that omits a lot for this example Login ID: edit has focus Password: edit protected ``` ### Anything else? This is my first thought and I'm quite sure it needs refinement. This could also be an accessibility bug in the "autofocus" attribute because of the way screen readers process it, but I think that creating a new attribute would avoid breaking existing behavior that's been worked around.
